note.en: What you see: At the same withdrawn station as the short axis, the plane turns lengthwise so the outflow tract, valve and proximal ascending aorta line up in one channel. Two cusps hinge at the annulus with the sinuses bulging behind them and the sinotubular junction marking where the root meets the tubular aorta. The left atrium lies behind the root. This is the measuring plane for the annulus, sinuses and junction, and for aligning Doppler with the jet.

steps.en: What you see: At the same withdrawn station as the short axis, the plane turns lengthwise so the outflow tract, valve and proximal ascending aorta line up in one channel. Two cusps hinge at the annulus with the sinuses bulging behind them and the sinotubular junction marking where the root meets the tubular aorta. The left atrium lies behind the root. This is the measuring plane for the annulus, sinuses and junction, and for aligning Doppler with the jet.

Landmarks to confirm: Left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root with sinuses of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, proximal ascending aorta, left and non coronary cusps, left atrium cavity, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

Common mistakes and correction: Off axis cut that overstates cusp thickness: fine tune the angle until the walls run parallel. Sitting too low so the valve drops out: withdraw slightly back to the withdrawn station. Near field clutter hiding a root abscess in suspected endocarditis: lower near gain and sweep slowly through the root before judging.

Normal values with units: Probe depth about 25 to 30 cm from the incisors. Multiplane angle near 120 degrees, accepted between 110 and 135 degrees. Dimensions are taken in mid systole at the annulus, sinuses and sinotubular junction. A peak jet velocity of 4.0 m per s or above, or a mean gradient of 40 mmHg or above, marks severe stenosis.

Pitfalls: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so combined aortic and mitral thickening in a young patient should be recorded as possible multivalve rheumatic disease. Foreshortened roots understate annular size before intervention, so confirm the longest root length before measuring. Mobile strands on the valve need slow motion review to separate vegetation from artefact.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: From the aortic valve short axis at about 25 to 30 cm, rotate the multiplane forward toward 120 degrees without advancing or withdrawing. Stop when the outflow tract looks longest and the anterior and posterior walls run parallel. Centre the annulus and freeze in mid systole for dimensions. If the valve vanishes, sweep slowly between 110 and 135 degrees until the root returns to full length.

remember.en: Measure the root levels and align Doppler with the jet

q.en: How is the aortic valve long axis obtained from the short axis station?

why.en: Rotation toward 120 degrees at the same withdrawn station opens the root lengthwise.

q.en: Which landmark marks the top of the aortic root?

o.en: The sinotubular junction where the root meets the tubular aorta

why.en: The sinotubular junction marks where the sinuses end and the tubular aorta begins.

q.en: Which Doppler value marks severe aortic stenosis?

o.en: Peak velocity below 2.0 m per s

why.en: A mean gradient of 40 mmHg or above marks severe stenosis.
